title: Geometric strict henselization over a prime localization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ a geometric point with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point]. Write $H$ for its geometric strict henselization ring [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Let $b:R\to H$ be a ring homomorphism whose spectrum is the structural morphism [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. There exist a prime ideal $q\subset R$, a field $K$ which is a separable closure of the residue field of $A=R_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], compatible residue-field and $A$-algebra structures on $K$, and an $A$-algebra structure on $H$ such that $A\to H$ composed with $R\to A$ equals $b$, and $H$ is an algebraic strict henselization of $A$ relative to $K$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization].

proof.text: Apply the affine neighbourhood/triples comparison to the identity chart of Spec R. Its prime is the image of the geometric point and K is the relative separable closure of its scheme residue field in Omega. Keep the comparison of ring diagrams and the specified equations for structural R-maps and colimit legs.

Use the canonical colimit cocone k of the small affine coordinate-ring diagram, whose vertex is the given strict henselization ring. The representative equivalence transports the affine-neighbourhood cocone cn to a universal cocone on this diagram. Uniqueness of colimits gives eN: cn.pt isomorphic to k.pt, explicitly specifying the target cocone k both in the isomorphism and its leg formula. Compose the inverse chart/triples colimit comparison with eN.

The identity residue triple maps to every triple by its structural map. Cocone naturality makes the transported R-map bprime independent of the triple. Evaluate the comparison at one small representative. The specified structural-map equation of the affine/triples equivalence, its colimit-leg equation, and the leg formula for eN express bprime through that representative. Naturality of toSpecGamma and the representative structural-map characterization give Spec.map bprime = the strict-henselization structural map. Faithfulness of Spec and hb give bprime = b.

Apply the localized strict-henselization theorem to the universal triple cocone, the constructed isomorphism and the common structural R-map. It returns the compatible local-base algebra structures and strict henselization property. Set q = p.asIdeal and use bprime = b in the elementwise structural-map equation.

theorem strictHenselizationRing_local_presentation
    (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (barY : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec R)
    (b : R ⟶ strictHenselizationRing barY)
    (hb : Spec.map b = strictHenselizationStructuralMap barY) :
    ∃ (q : Ideal R) (_ : q.IsPrime)
      (K : Type u) (_ : Field K)
      (_ : Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q)) K)
      (_ : IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q)) K)
      (_ : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime q) K)
      (_ : IsScalarTower (Localization.AtPrime q)
        (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q)) K)
      (_ : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime q) (strictHenselizationRing barY)),
      (∀ r : R, algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime q) (strictHenselizationRing barY)
        (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q) r) = b.hom r) ∧
      Algebra.IsStrictHenselization (Localization.AtPrime q) K
        (strictHenselizationRing barY)
